Mesillat Yesharim 2:8: However, this is truly one of the stratagems and cunning of the evil inclination — to weigh down its labor continually upon the hearts of men, so that no respite is left them to reflect and consider along what path they are walking.
Mesillat Yesharim 2:9: For it knows that if they were to pay even the slightest attention to their ways, they would certainly immediately begin to regret their deeds, and this regret would keep growing stronger within them until they would abandon sin entirely.
Mesillat Yesharim 2:10: And this is much like the counsel of the wicked Pharaoh, who said (Exodus 5:9): "Let the labor be heavier upon the men, etc." — for he intended thereby to leave them no respite at all, so that they would not take heed or devise any plan against him, but rather he strove to disturb their hearts from all reflection by the force of unceasing, continuous labor.
Mesillat Yesharim 2:11: Such, precisely, is the counsel of the evil inclination toward the sons of man; for it is a man of war, skilled in cunning, and it is impossible to escape it except through great wisdom and profound reflection. This is what the prophet cries out and says (Haggai 1:5): "Set your heart upon your ways."
Mesillat Yesharim 2:12: And Solomon said in his wisdom (Proverbs 6:4-5): "Give not sleep to your eyes, nor slumber to your eyelids; deliver yourself as a gazelle from the hand, etc."
Mesillat Yesharim 2:13: And our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Moed Katan 5a): "Whoever sets his ways in this world merits to see the salvation of the Holy One, blessed be He."
Mesillat Yesharim 2:14: And it is obvious that even if a person keeps watch over himself, he lacks the power to be saved unless the Holy One, blessed be He, helps him, for the evil inclination is very powerful, as Scripture says (Psalms 37:32-33): "The wicked watches for the righteous, and seeks to slay him; the Lord will not abandon him, etc."
Mesillat Yesharim 2:15: But if a person keeps watch over himself, then the Holy One, blessed be He, helps him, and he is delivered from the evil inclination.
Mesillat Yesharim 2:16: But if he does not keep watch over himself, then certainly the Holy One, blessed be He, will not keep watch over him. For if he does not have pity on himself, who will have pity on him? This is like the matter of which our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Berachot 33a): "Whoever lacks understanding, it is forbidden to have mercy on him." And this is what they said (Avot 1:14): "If I am not for myself, who will be for me?"
Mesillat Yesharim 3:1:
An Explanation of the Components of Watchfulness
Now, one who wishes to keep watch over himself needs two kinds of reflection:
Mesillat Yesharim 3:2: The first, that he reflect on what is the true good that a person should choose, and the true evil from which he should flee.
Mesillat Yesharim 3:3: And the second, on the deeds that he does, to see whether they belong to the category of the good or to the category of the evil.
Mesillat Yesharim 3:4: And this, both at the time of the deed and not at the time of the deed.
Mesillat Yesharim 3:5: At the time of the deed — that he do no deed at all without weighing it in the scales of this knowledge.
Mesillat Yesharim 3:6: And not at the time of the deed — that he bring to mind the sum total of his deeds and likewise weigh them in the scales of this reckoning, to see what evil is found in them, so as to reject it, and what good, so as to persist in it and strengthen himself in it. And if he finds evil among them, he should then reflect and search out in his mind what stratagem he should employ to turn away from that evil and to purify himself from it.
Mesillat Yesharim 3:7: And this our Sages, of blessed memory, made known to us when they said (Eruvin 13b): "It would have been better for man not to have been created than to have been created; but now that he has been created, let him examine his deeds" — and some say, "let him feel over his deeds." And you will see that both expressions are two good and very useful cautions.
Mesillat Yesharim 3:8: For "examining" one's deeds means to investigate and reflect upon one's deeds as a whole, to see whether there are found among them deeds that ought not to be done, that do not follow the commandments and statutes of the Lord — for whatever he finds of these, he should eradicate from the world.
Mesillat Yesharim 3:9: But "feeling over" is an investigation even into one's good deeds themselves, to inquire and see whether there is in their nature some improper intention, or some evil element which needs to be removed and eradicated.
Mesillat Yesharim 3:10: And this is like one who feels over a garment to test whether it is sound and strong or weak and worn out; so too he should feel over his deeds, to examine their quality with the utmost discernment, until they remain pure and clean.
Mesillat Yesharim 3:11: The general rule of the matter is: a person should examine all his deeds, and keep watch over all his ways, so as not to allow himself a bad habit or a bad character trait, all the more so a transgression or a sin.
Mesillat Yesharim 3:12: And I see it as necessary for a person to be exacting and to weigh his ways day by day, like great merchants who constantly balance all their accounts so that they do not become confused; and he should set fixed times and hours for this, so that his reckoning is not haphazard but firmly established, for its consequences are far-reaching.
Mesillat Yesharim 3:13: And our Sages, of blessed memory, taught us explicitly the need for this reckoning, in what they said, of blessed memory (Bava Batra 78b):
Mesillat Yesharim 3:14: "Therefore the poets say, come to Cheshbon" (Numbers 21:27) — therefore those who rule over their inclination say: come, let us calculate the reckoning of the world — the loss incurred by a mitzvah against its reward, and the reward of a transgression against its loss, and so on.
Mesillat Yesharim 3:15: And this is because this true counsel can only be given, and its truth recognized, by those who have already emerged from under the hand of their inclination and have gained mastery over it. For one who is still imprisoned in the captivity of his inclination — his eyes do not see this truth and he cannot recognize it, for the inclination truly blinds his eyes; and he is like one walking in the dark, before whom there are obstacles, but his eyes do not see them.
Mesillat Yesharim 3:16: And this is what they said, of blessed memory (Bava Metzia 83b): "You appoint darkness, and it is night" (Psalms 104:20) — this refers to this world, which resembles the night.
Mesillat Yesharim 3:17: And understand how wondrous this true statement is, for one who probes deeply to understand it. For the darkness of night can cause two kinds of error to a person's eye: either it covers the eye so that it does not see what is before it at all, or it deceives it so that it sees a post as though it were a man, and a man as though he were a post.
Mesillat Yesharim 3:18: So too, the materiality and corporeality of this world are the darkness of night to the eye of the intellect, and cause it two kinds of error:
Mesillat Yesharim 3:19: the first, it does not let it see the obstacles that lie along the ways of the world,
Mesillat Yesharim 3:20: and so fools are found walking along securely and stumbling and perishing, without any fear having come upon them beforehand. This is what Scripture says (Proverbs 4:19): "The way of the wicked is like darkness; they know not at what they stumble." And it says (ibid. 22:3): "The prudent man sees evil and hides himself, but the simple pass on and are punished." And it says (ibid. 14:16): "But the fool rages and is confident," for their hearts are as sound to them as a great hall, and they fall before they know of the obstacle at all.
Mesillat Yesharim 3:21: And the second error, which is more severe than the first, is that it deceives their sight until they see evil as though it were actually good, and good as though it were evil, and because of this they strengthen themselves and persist in their evil deeds. For it is not enough that they lack the sight of truth to see the evil that lies before their faces, but it even appears to them that they find great proofs and demonstrative tests for their evil opinions and their false beliefs,
Mesillat Yesharim 3:22: and this is the great evil that ensnares them and brings them to the pit of destruction. This is what Scripture says (Isaiah 6:10): "Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes, lest..."
Mesillat Yesharim 3:23: And all this is because they are under the darkness and subjugated under the dominion of their inclination. But those who have already emerged from this imprisonment — they see the truth as it truly is, and are able to counsel the rest of mankind concerning it.
Mesillat Yesharim 3:24: To what may this be compared? To a labyrinth garden — the garden planted for amusement, well known among noblemen, in which the plantings form walls upon walls, and among them many paths, confused and intertwined, all resembling one another,
Mesillat Yesharim 3:25: and the goal within them is to reach a single pavilion at their center. Now, some of these paths are straight and truly lead to the pavilion, while others mislead a person and take him further away from it.
Mesillat Yesharim 3:26: And indeed, one who walks among the paths cannot see or know at all whether he is on the true path or the false one, for they are all alike, with no difference between them to the eye of the one looking at them — unless he already knows the way through expertise and a practiced eye, having already entered these paths and reached the goal, which is the pavilion.
Mesillat Yesharim 3:27: Now, one who already stands upon the pavilion sees all the paths before him and can distinguish between the true ones and the false ones, and he is able to caution those walking along them, saying: This is the way, walk in it!
Mesillat Yesharim 3:28: And behold, whoever is willing to believe him will reach the appointed place. But whoever is unwilling to believe him and wishes to follow his own eyes will certainly remain lost and will not reach it.
Mesillat Yesharim 3:29: So it is with this matter: whoever has not yet gained mastery over his inclination is still among the paths and cannot distinguish between them. But those who have mastered their inclination and have already reached the pavilion — who have already emerged from the paths and see all the ways clearly before their eyes — they are able to advise whoever wishes to listen, and it is they whom we need to believe.
Mesillat Yesharim 3:30: And indeed, what is the counsel that they give us? "Come to the reckoning; come, let us calculate the reckoning of the world" — for they have already tested, seen, and known that this alone is the true way for a person to reach the good that he seeks, and no other.
Mesillat Yesharim 3:31: In sum: a person must always reflect with his mind, at every time, and at a fixed time set aside for solitary reflection, on what is the true path, according to the law of the Torah, that a person needs to walk in. And afterward he should come to reflect upon his own deeds, whether they follow this path or not; for through this it will surely be easy for him to purify himself from all evil and to straighten all his ways. And as Scripture says (Proverbs 4:26): "Make level the path of your feet, and let all your ways be firmly established." And it says (Lamentations 3:40): "Let us search and examine our ways, and turn back to the Lord."
